title: Data model design for an app
when: Before building an app that stores records (tasks, orders, members, bookings), or when the data shape is messy and needs a redesign.
prompt:
Goal: A written model of entities, fields, relations and rules that code, storage and API all follow.
Steps:
1. Take the nouns of the request; those with their own life cycle become entities (Customer, Order, OrderLine), the rest become fields.
2. Per entity: fields with type, required, default, limits and an example; always id (UUID string), createdAt, updatedAt as ISO strings.
3. One to many by a foreign id on the many side (order.customerId); many to many through a join entity with its own fields.
4. Store facts and derive the rest (quantity and unitPriceCents, not totals); status as an enum with allowed transitions.
5. Normalize stored data; denormalize only for rebuildable view caches. Decide soft or hard delete and cascades.
6. Write sample JSON per entity and a format version.
Quality bar:
- Every field serves a feature.
- Consistent naming (camelCase fields, singular entities).
- Money in integer minor units, dates in ISO 8601.
Pitfalls:
- Stored totals that drift from their lines.
- Names or emails used as ids.
- Deep nesting edited from several places.
Verify:
- [ ] Each entity lists fields, types and an example.
- [ ] Relations and delete rules stated.
- [ ] Status transitions documented.
- [ ] Sample JSON parses.
Output: docs/data-model.md with a section per entity and data/sample.json with example records.

examples.input: planeja os dados de um app de agendamento de salão
examples.output: Client, Professional, Service, Appointment with status transitions, priceCents, sample.json
